rows.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view — paragraph 1
Chart data: revenue and EBITDA — paragraph 1

limitations: Produced in a host session and accepted by the CP-OS check.
Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

- EBITDA is not stated by the issuer in any period, so EBITDA (Reported) is derived as operating income plus depreciation and amortization; every leverage and cover ratio depends on that definition. Severity: Medium. Action: none possible from the filings. - Adjusted EBITDA and its add-back list are not stated, so the adjusted ratios and the EBITDA bridge are not supplied. Severity: Medium. Action: none possible from the filings. - The credit facility's required financial ratios are described but no test level, step-down or definition is printed, so covenant headroom is not calculable. Severity: High. Action: obtain the executed credit agreement and compliance certificates. - No statements after 30 June 2026 are supplied, although the as-of date is 141 days later; the July 2026 borrowing of USD 301.3 million and repurchase of USD 273.7 million are stated without a resulting balance, so pro forma net debt rests on the repurchase cost alone, ignores other July cash flows and has no stated day. Severity: High. Action: supply the fourth-quarter FY2026 report if issued. - Cash interest paid for FY2024 and FY2025 is stated only in USD millions to one decimal, so the FY2025 and last-twelve-months interest cover carry that rounding. Severity: Low. Action: none needed for the snapshot. - Letters of credit and bank guarantees are stated at 2025-09-30 and 2024-09-30 but not at 30 June 2026, and unused revolver commitments of USD 774.9 million exceed the USD 757.5 million available to borrow by USD 17.4 million for a reason the filing does not give. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the facility compliance or borrowing-base detail. - Items outside debt at 30 June 2026 total USD 159,602 thousand, an unpaid solar energy investment of USD 134,602 thousand and a repurchase executed but not settled of USD 25,000 thousand, and the settlement dates are not stated. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the payment timing from management. - Several statement lines are Not supplied in some periods because the filing prints a dash or does not present the line in that period: impairment and other charges in nine months 2026, the gain on divestiture in the fiscal years and nine months 2025, deferred income taxes in the nine-month columns, the solar energy contribution and divestiture proceeds before 2026, other investing activities, repayments of senior notes in FY2024 and nine months 2026, repurchases of common stock in FY2024, credit facility origination costs and deferred acquisition consideration. No zero is implied. Severity: Low. Action: none needed. - No segment revenue schedule exists because the issuer reports one operating and reportable segment; revenue by line of business is printed in the filings but is not a segment and is not summed here. Severity: Low. Action: none. - Carrying value by debt instrument is not stated, so each instrument is carried at principal with one financing cost adjustment for the senior notes; issuance costs of the revolver and term loan sit in other assets and are not netted from debt. Severity: Low. Action: none needed. - The spread over the base rate and any floor on the credit facility are not stated, and the exact maturity day of the 2028 senior notes is not stated. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the credit agreement and indenture. - The KPI dashboard shows Not supplied for revenue growth in nine months 2025 because nine months 2024 is not in the file set, and for ARR excluding divested businesses at the fiscal year ends because that basis starts in fiscal 2026. Severity: Low. Action: none needed. - Finance lease amounts are not stated because finance leases are carried within property and equipment and other balance sheet lines; pension and purchase obligation figures are available only at FY2025. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the lease and pension notes of the next annual report. - Discrete quarters Q1, Q2 and Q3 of FY2026 and a standalone fourth quarter of FY2025 are not tabulated; the nine-month and annual columns are. Severity: Low. Action: build discrete quarters from the quarterly reports if a quarterly view is needed. - The interim quarterly reports and releases are unaudited and the filings state no auditor review, so nine-month figures carry lower evidence quality than the annual figures. Severity: Low. Action: none.

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against treating buybacks as a creditor risk is that management repaid debt before the repurchase wave and still holds large undrawn bank capacity: net debt repayments were USD 553 million in FY2025 and USD 757.5 million of the revolver was available to borrow at 30 June 2026. The view would soften if the fourth-quarter FY2026 report shows repurchases slowing to the level of free cash flow, and harden if borrowing keeps funding repurchases beyond the guided total. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a positive view concerns policy, not performance. Management showed within nine months that it will add debt to buy back stock: the Q3 2026 repurchase of USD 525 million was more than twice the quarter's earlier target, and the July 2026 repurchase was financed mainly by new borrowing. If that continued until the revolver was used up, total debt would reach 1.79x last-twelve-months EBITDA on the amounts stated at 30 June 2026, and a repeat of the Q3 2026 revenue shortfall would raise the ratio further because operating expenses did not flex. Operating expenses were also held flat partly by transition services income, which the issuer provides for up to 12 months from the sale. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The realistic downside starts with tariff-driven weakness among manufacturing customers, who delay purchases and shorten renewals. License revenue, which is recognised when a contract starts, falls first, as it did in Q3 2026 when revenue fell 6.82% and operating income fell 20.65% because operating expenses did not flex. Free cash flow then weakens, annual billing in advance means less cash is collected from smaller contract values, and if repurchases continue beyond free cash flow the revolver supplies the difference; drawing all of the amount available to borrow would take total debt to 1.79x EBITDA on the June 2026 amounts. Management can stop repurchases, which are discretionary, and capital expenditure is small, so resilience looks sufficient to avoid liquidity distress unless repurchases continue into the 2027 refinancing window. License revenue, which is recognised when a contract starts, falls first, as it did in Q3 2026 when revenue fell 6.82% and operating income fell 20.65% because operating expenses did not flex. Free cash flow then weakens, annual billing in advance means less cash is collected from smaller contract values, and if repurchases continue beyond free cash flow the revolver supplies the difference; drawing all of the amount available to borrow would take total debt to 1.79x EBITDA on the June 2026 amounts. Management can stop repurchases, which are discretionary, and capital expenditure is small, so resilience looks sufficient to avoid liquidity distress unless repurchases continue into the 2027 refinancing window.

facts.text: Overall, Ptc Inc. presents a strong business profile supported by recurring subscription revenue, high margins and low leverage, but credit quality is constrained by debt-funded repurchases and a single fiscal 2028 maturity window. Cash-flow durability appears strong because free cash flow was 0.77x EBITDA over the last twelve months and guided FY2026 free cash flow is about USD 850 million. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on whether net debt stays near the 0.88x EBITDA of June 2026, or the 1.11x pro forma for the July 2026 repurchase, until the facility becomes current on 2027-01-03. The primary downside path is repurchases funded by the revolver while revenue timing weakens results. Against typical leveraged-credit issuers in software, low leverage is a point of difference, but no peer set is supplied, so the comparison is not established. ## Findings
### Bottom line

Net debt was only 0.88x last-twelve-months EBITDA at 30 June 2026, but borrowing to fund buybacks has begun to reverse the earlier deleveraging, so creditor protection rests on cash flow and management's capital-allocation choices rather than on covenant levels the filings do not state.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C7; calculation C8

Total debt was 1.17x and cash interest paid was covered 20.53x on the same basis, against 2.51x and 5.08x at FY2024. A July 2026 repurchase of USD 273.7 million financed by USD 301.3 million of net borrowings is outside those ratios; it lifts pro forma net leverage to 1.11x.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation C27; calculation C28
### Key findings

Reported leverage fell sharply in FY2025 and has edged up since. Total debt to EBITDA was 2.51x at FY2024, 1.10x at FY2025 and 1.17x at 30 June 2026, while net debt to EBITDA moved from 2.13x to 0.93x to 0.88x. FY2025 combined EBITDA growth with net debt repayments of USD 553 million; the nine months to June 2026 then added net borrowings of USD 225 million to help fund repurchases of USD 1,326 million.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_ptc-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 58–61; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 2–5; calculation C32; calculation C31; calculation C33

Cash interest paid was covered 5.08x at FY2024, 13.94x at FY2025 and 20.53x on a last-twelve-months basis, because EBITDA grew and cash interest paid fell to USD 40,543 thousand in the nine months to June 2026 from USD 59,062 thousand a year earlier. Cash interest paid for the two fiscal years is stated only to USD 0.1 million, so the FY2025 and last-twelve-months cover carry that rounding, and the July 2026 borrowing is not yet in cash interest.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_ptc-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 89; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_ptc-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 12; calculation C18

Cash conversion is strong but not constant. Free cash flow, defined as operating cash flow less additions to property and equipment, was 0.79x EBITDA in FY2025 and 0.77x over the last twelve months, and FY2025 carried an outflow of USD 195,767 thousand in other noncurrent assets and liabilities. Deferred revenue of USD 700,298 thousand at 30 June 2026 is the issuer's main non-debt funding, since customers are generally invoiced annually in advance, and it was USD 111,973 thousand lower than at 30 September 2025.

Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_ptc-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 32; calculation C40; calculation C41; calculation C34

Liquidity at 30 June 2026 was cash of USD 351,454 thousand plus unused revolver commitments of USD 774.9 million, of which USD 757.5 million was available to borrow, against a USD 1.25 billion revolver. Both the facility and the 2028 notes fall due in fiscal 2028, so USD 1,393.7 million of the USD 1,425.0 million of scheduled principal matures in that year. Only USD 25,074 thousand of debt is classified as current and no facility matures within twelve months of 30 June 2026. Two items outside debt were unpaid at that date, a solar energy investment of USD 134,602 thousand and a repurchase of USD 25,000 thousand executed but not settled, and their settlement dates are not established.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C19; calculation C20; calculation C39

The issuer states no EBITDA or adjusted EBITDA, so every ratio uses EBITDA derived as operating income plus depreciation and amortization, which treats stock-based compensation of USD 185,848 thousand in the nine months to June 2026 as a cost. The issuer's non-GAAP operating income was USD 285.4 million above GAAP operating income in that period, so issuer-adjusted leverage would look lower than the figures here.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 24; calculation C4; calculation C36

The sale of Kepware and ThingWorx is reported with several figures that serve different purposes. Total consideration was USD 530.8 million and cash received was USD 523.3 million; the gain was USD 462.6 million in other income and USD 464.6 million in the cash flow statement, which adds USD 2.0 million from an earlier divestiture; tax on the sale was USD 95.6 million. Operating income excludes the gain, so EBITDA is not inflated by it, but nine-month net income is.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_ptc-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation C38

Several claims sit outside the debt figure. Operating lease obligations were USD 184,379 thousand at 30 June 2026 on their own balance sheet lines, and the headquarters lease runs to 2037; the defined benefit pension projected benefit obligation was USD 69,460 thousand at FY2025; purchase obligations were USD 188.8 million at FY2025, of which USD 91.9 million fell in FY2026; and legal proceedings are described as immaterial. No factoring or supplier finance programme is described in the sources read, and finance leases sit in other balance sheet lines without a stated amount.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2025-09-30_ptc-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-K_2025-09-30_ptc-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 90; 10-K_2025-09-30_ptc-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 95; 10-K_2025-09-30_ptc-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 100; calculation C37; calculation C42; calculation C43
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest contrary evidence is that last-twelve-months EBITDA still includes Kepware and ThingWorx until their sale in March 2026, a business with USD 46 million of revenue in Q3 2025 alone, so leverage on the continuing business is higher than 1.17x; the July 2026 borrowing then adds to net debt. The view would worsen if repurchases keep being funded from the revolver, and improve if the fourth-quarter FY2026 report shows net debt back near its FY2025 level.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 24; calculation C27

## Gaps

- EBITDA is not stated by the issuer in any period, so EBITDA (Reported) is derived as operating income plus depreciation and amortization; every leverage and cover ratio depends on that definition. Severity: Medium. Action: none possible from the filings.
- Adjusted EBITDA and its add-back list are not stated, so the adjusted ratios and the EBITDA bridge are not supplied. Severity: Medium. Action: none possible from the filings.

- The credit facility's required financial ratios are described but no test level, step-down or definition is printed, so covenant headroom is not calculable. Severity: High. Action: obtain the executed credit agreement and compliance certificates.

- No statements after 30 June 2026 are supplied, although the as-of date is 141 days later; the July 2026 borrowing of USD 301.3 million and repurchase of USD 273.7 million are stated without a resulting balance, so pro forma net debt rests on the repurchase cost alone, ignores other July cash flows and has no stated day. Severity: High. Action: supply the fourth-quarter FY2026 report if issued.

- Cash interest paid for FY2024 and FY2025 is stated only in USD millions to one decimal, so the FY2025 and last-twelve-months interest cover carry that rounding. Severity: Low. Action: none needed for the snapshot.

- Letters of credit and bank guarantees are stated at 2025-09-30 and 2024-09-30 but not at 30 June 2026, and unused revolver commitments of USD 774.9 million exceed the USD 757.5 million available to borrow by USD 17.4 million for a reason the filing does not give. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the facility compliance or borrowing-base detail.

- Items outside debt at 30 June 2026 total USD 159,602 thousand, an unpaid solar energy investment of USD 134,602 thousand and a repurchase executed but not settled of USD 25,000 thousand, and the settlement dates are not stated. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the payment timing from management.

- Several statement lines are Not supplied in some periods because the filing prints a dash or does not present the line in that period: impairment and other charges in nine months 2026, the gain on divestiture in the fiscal years and nine months 2025, deferred income taxes in the nine-month columns, the solar energy contribution and divestiture proceeds before 2026, other investing activities, repayments of senior notes in FY2024 and nine months 2026, repurchases of common stock in FY2024, credit facility origination costs and deferred acquisition consideration. No zero is implied. Severity: Low. Action: none needed.

- No segment revenue schedule exists because the issuer reports one operating and reportable segment; revenue by line of business is printed in the filings but is not a segment and is not summed here. Severity: Low. Action: none.

- Carrying value by debt instrument is not stated, so each instrument is carried at principal with one financing cost adjustment for the senior notes; issuance costs of the revolver and term loan sit in other assets and are not netted from debt. Severity: Low. Action: none needed.

- The spread over the base rate and any floor on the credit facility are not stated, and the exact maturity day of the 2028 senior notes is not stated. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the credit agreement and indenture.

- The KPI dashboard shows Not supplied for revenue growth in nine months 2025 because nine months 2024 is not in the file set, and for ARR excluding divested businesses at the fiscal year ends because that basis starts in fiscal 2026. Severity: Low. Action: none needed.

- Finance lease amounts are not stated because finance leases are carried within property and equipment and other balance sheet lines; pension and purchase obligation figures are available only at FY2025. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the lease and pension notes of the next annual report.

- Discrete quarters Q1, Q2 and Q3 of FY2026 and a standalone fourth quarter of FY2025 are not tabulated; the nine-month and annual columns are. Severity: Low. Action: build discrete quarters from the quarterly reports if a quarterly view is needed.

- The interim quarterly reports and releases are unaudited and the filings state no auditor review, so nine-month figures carry lower evidence quality than the annual figures. Severity: Low. Action: none.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Ptc Inc. is a widely held subscription software company with no sponsor or controlling shareholder identified in the filings, so creditor risk comes from management's capital-allocation policy, which has swung from debt repayment in FY2025 to debt-funded buybacks in FY2026.

About 95% of revenue is recurring and no customer exceeds 10% of revenue, which supports cash flow, but the March 2026 sale of Kepware and ThingWorx removed part of the revenue base, and the ownership, board and related-party detail held in the proxy statement is not supplied.
### Key findings

The franchise is a single-segment design and product-data software business with broad diversification, which supports debt service. PLM was 62.27% and CAD 37.73% of FY2025 software revenue, the Americas, Europe and Asia Pacific generated 48.45%, 36.33% and 15.22% of FY2025 revenue, no customer exceeded 10% of revenue or receivables, and about 75% of sales are made directly.

Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_ptc-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-09-30_ptc-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-K_2025-09-30_ptc-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 65; 10-K_2025-09-30_ptc-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 76; calculation C1; calculation C3

Ownership offers no sponsor-extraction channel, but control and board rights are not established. The shares are widely held, with a few hundred holders of record at 30 September 2025, and buybacks cut shares outstanding by 7.38% between 30 September 2025 and 30 June 2026; any holder of more than five percent, the board and related-party dealings sit in a proxy statement that is not supplied.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_ptc-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-K_2025-09-30_ptc-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 51; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C6

Management's stated policy is to return excess cash to shareholders, and in FY2026 that policy has been funded partly with debt. The sale brought in USD 523.3 million of cash and a USD 375 million accelerated repurchase was funded from the proceeds, open-market repurchases continued, and the July 2026 repurchase of USD 273.7 million was financed mainly by USD 301.3 million of net borrowings. Guided FY2026 repurchases of about USD 1,625 million exceed guided free cash flow plus the sale cash by USD 251.7 million.

Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_ptc-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-K_2025-09-30_ptc-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 21; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_ptc-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C8

Acquisitions have been funded from bank debt that was later reduced, which links growth to bank capacity. ServiceMax cost USD 1,448.2 million net of cash in January 2023 and was funded with USD 630 million of revolver and USD 500 million of term loan borrowing, which also repaid the prior facility; pure-systems cost USD 93.5 million in October 2023 and was financed mainly by a revolver draw; the IncQuery purchase of USD 7.9 million in 2025 was small. The March 2026 sale of Kepware and ThingWorx is a disposal of part of the portfolio and not an acquisition.

Cash flow is steady but reported revenue is lumpy. Under the revenue recognition standard the licence portion of an on-premises subscription is recognised when the contract starts, so Q3 2026 licence revenue fell by 18% on a single large renewal of shortened duration while support and cloud revenue held, and about 95% of revenue is recurring.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 25; calculation C9

Disclosure supports monitoring of results but not of covenants. The annual accounts carry an audit opinion from PricewaterhouseCoopers that the statements present fairly, and the issuer reports ARR, non-GAAP reconciliations and quarterly guidance, but covenant levels, compliance certificates and the credit agreement are not in the sources. Total deferred revenue also fell with the divestiture, by about USD 56 million, which explains part of the fall in the balance since 30 September 2025.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_ptc-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 58; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation C7
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against treating buybacks as a creditor risk is that management repaid debt before the repurchase wave and still holds large undrawn bank capacity: net debt repayments were USD 553 million in FY2025 and USD 757.5 million of the revolver was available to borrow at 30 June 2026. The view would soften if the fourth-quarter FY2026 report shows repurchases slowing to the level of free cash flow, and harden if borrowing keeps funding repurchases beyond the guided total.
### Limitations

- The proxy statement is not supplied, so the conclusion that no sponsor or controlling shareholder exists rests on the absence of any such disclosure in the filings and would change if a holder of more than five percent were found.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_ptc-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 51

- The credit agreement and note indenture are not supplied, so the conclusion that debt-funded buybacks are a creditor risk rests on observed behaviour and not on legal capacity to distribute, which is not established.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_ptc-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 88

The 2025 senior notes were redeemed in fiscal 2025 using a revolver draw and cash on hand, which left the 2028 senior notes and the bank facility as the only debt, and the bank facility was amended on 18 November 2025 to remove the asset-sale restriction for the Kepware and ThingWorx sale and to permit other asset sales of up to USD 250 million of book value in a fiscal year.

The dates of the agreement, the closing and the financing events are recorded in the Source readiness events.

# Fundamental credit: Ptc Inc. (ptc-857005), as of 2026-11-18
## Request

Fundamental credit assessment of Ptc Inc. (issuer id ptc-857005), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the eight supplied filings and releases and the Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance outputs. No rating, security recommendation, covenant or recovery conclusion is made here.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Ptc Inc. has a strong fundamental credit profile, built on recurring software revenue and low leverage, so creditors are well covered today, but the buyback policy and a single fiscal 2028 maturity window are the real risks to that position.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 31; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C6

Net debt was 0.88x last-twelve-months EBITDA at 30 June 2026 and 1.11x pro forma for the USD 273.7 million July 2026 repurchase, whose day is not stated, and free cash flow was 0.77x EBITDA over the last twelve months. USD 1,393.7 million of USD 1,425.0 million of scheduled principal falls due in fiscal 2028. Guided FY2026 repurchases of USD 1,625 million exceed guided free cash flow and sale cash by USD 251.7 million.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 21; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_ptc-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C4; calculation C7; calculation C5; calculation C26
### Key findings

The revenue base is recurring and diversified, which makes debt service predictable. About 95% of revenue is recurring, no customer exceeded 10% of revenue, about 75% of sales are made directly, and annual run rate excluding the divested businesses grew 7% to USD 2,412.4 million at 30 June 2026. Management expects churn to remain low, but a retention rate is not disclosed.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-K_2025-09-30_ptc-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-09-30_ptc-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 65; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_ptc-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C17

Margins and cash conversion are high, and Q3 2026 showed how fast earnings fall when revenue slips. Reported EBITDA margin was 39.61% in FY2025 and 36.77% in the nine months to June 2026, and free cash flow was 0.77x EBITDA over the last twelve months. Part of the FY2025 margin reflects up-front license recognition on longer contracts, because revenue grew 19.18% while annual run rate grew 9.93%. In Q3 2026 revenue fell 6.82% and operating income fell 20.65% because operating expenses stayed flat, a margin loss of about 480 basis points.

Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_ptc-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-K_2025-09-30_ptc-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 24; calculation C10; calculation C13; calculation C14; calculation C15; calculation C7

Leverage is low and interest cover is wide, so debt service is not the near-term constraint. Net debt was 0.88x last-twelve-months EBITDA at 30 June 2026 and 1.11x pro forma for the July 2026 repurchase, against 0.93x at FY2025 and 2.13x at FY2024. EBITDA covered cash interest paid 20.53x, and would still cover it 16.37x if the July 2026 net borrowing carried the 5.0% rate stated for the credit facility.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 21; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C31

The binding constraint is a single maturity window and not the annual cash need. Scheduled principal of USD 1,425.0 million is due almost entirely in fiscal 2028, USD 1,393.7 million or 97.80%, because the revolver and term loan mature on 2028-01-03 and the fixed-rate senior notes in February 2028. The facility becomes a current liability from 2027-01-03, so the refinancing question reaches the balance sheet at 2027-03-31. The notes were quoted at 98.00% of face value on 30 June 2026, which does not by itself signal market stress.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 19; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C34; calculation C29

Financial policy is the swing factor and turned against creditors in FY2026. FY2025 repaid USD 553 million of net debt, but repurchases of USD 1,326 million in the nine months to June 2026 and USD 273.7 million in July 2026 were funded in part by net borrowings of USD 225 million and USD 301.3 million. Guided FY2026 repurchases of USD 1,625 million exceed guided free cash flow plus sale cash by USD 251.7 million, so debt or cash on hand must fund the difference.

Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_ptc-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 31; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_ptc-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 4; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C28; calculation C26

The March 2026 sale of Kepware and ThingWorx shrank the revenue base and flatters the leverage ratios. Last-twelve-months EBITDA still includes the divested businesses, which produced USD 46 million of revenue in Q3 2025 alone, so leverage on the continuing business is higher than the 0.88x reported, before the July 2026 repurchase lifts net debt to 1.11x pro forma; the issuer guides FY2026 revenue at USD 2,690 million to USD 2,750 million, which is 2% lower to flat on FY2025.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 24; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_ptc-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 2; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C4

Covenant protection cannot be tested, so the view rests on cash flow and not on contractual headroom. The issuer states compliance with all financial and operating covenants at 30 June 2026 without giving the levels, and the facility's commitment fee depends on a total leverage ratio whose definition is not supplied.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 19; Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a positive view concerns policy, not performance. Management showed within nine months that it will add debt to buy back stock: the Q3 2026 repurchase of USD 525 million was more than twice the quarter's earlier target, and the July 2026 repurchase was financed mainly by new borrowing. If that continued until the revolver was used up, total debt would reach 1.79x last-twelve-months EBITDA on the amounts stated at 30 June 2026, and a repeat of the Q3 2026 revenue shortfall would raise the ratio further because operating expenses did not flex. Operating expenses were also held flat partly by transition services income, which the issuer provides for up to 12 months from the sale.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 28; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_ptc-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C32; calculation C14; calculation C35

Evidence in the other direction is that cash conversion stayed high through the divestiture year and that the issuer repaid debt before the repurchase wave. The view would improve if repurchases are held to free cash flow and net debt returns near its FY2025 level, and would worsen if guided annual run rate growth of 9% to 9.5% is missed, if net borrowing funds repurchases beyond the guided USD 1,625 million, or if a covenant amendment or waiver appears.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-07-29_ptc-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_ptc-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-09-30_ptc-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 34; calculation C25
### Limitations

- The conclusion that leverage is low uses EBITDA derived from statement lines, which includes the divested businesses until March 2026 and treats stock-based compensation as a cost, so the continuing-business ratio is higher and the issuer-adjusted ratio lower than the figures shown, by amounts that are not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 24; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- The conclusion that refinancing access is good rests on the leverage figures and a single quoted price for the 2028 notes, because no issuer rating, secondary loan price or peer set is supplied, and a rating action or wider spreads would change it.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 19; Source readiness (CP-0)

- The judgement that revenue is durable rests on the recurring share of revenue and on management's statement that churn is low, because renewal rates and customer cohort data are not disclosed, so a retention shortfall would not be visible until it reached revenue.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 22; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_ptc-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 4
### Strengths and weaknesses

The strongest support is cash generation from a recurring, diversified revenue base. About 95% of revenue is recurring, no customer exceeded 10% of revenue, and free cash flow of about USD 850 million is guided for FY2026 even after about USD 100 million of divestiture-related cash taxes. Debt principal equals 1.66 years of FY2025 free cash flow, so all of the debt could be repaid from internal cash flow in under two years if repurchases and other uses stopped.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-K_2025-09-30_ptc-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 65; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_ptc-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_ptc-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C9; calculation C25

Low leverage and a large undrawn revolver give creditors room to absorb a weak year. Net debt was 0.88x EBITDA and 1.11x pro forma for the July 2026 repurchase, cash was USD 351,454 thousand and USD 757.5 million was available to borrow under the revolver at 30 June 2026, before the July 2026 borrowing of USD 301.3 million, and the cash and availability after July 2026 are not established. Cash interest paid was covered 20.53x.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 21; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C4; calculation C3; calculation C8

The main weakness is a shareholder-return policy that the revolver is now funding. Repurchases of USD 1,326 million in the nine months to June 2026 and USD 273.7 million in July 2026 reversed the net debt repayments of FY2025, and the guided FY2026 repurchases of USD 1,625 million exceed guided free cash flow plus sale cash by USD 251.7 million. The issuer itself states that its credit facility limits could change the amount and timing of repurchases, but the limits are not supplied.

Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_ptc-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 23; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_ptc-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C26

Refinancing is concentrated in one window, and part of the debt is exposed to rates. USD 1,393.7 million or 97.80% of scheduled principal falls due in fiscal 2028, and 64.91% of principal is at a variable rate, where each change of 100 basis points costs about USD 9.25 million a year at the June 2026 balances. Revenue timing is lumpy because license revenue is recognised when a contract starts, as the Q3 2026 license decline of 18% on one renewal showed.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-K_2025-09-30_ptc-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 48; calculation C6; calculation C30; calculation C16

### Company description

Ptc Inc. sells design and product lifecycle software to manufacturers through one reportable segment, and the subscription model supports cash-flow visibility and debt service. Product lifecycle management was 62.27% and computer-aided design 37.73% of FY2025 software revenue, and the Americas, Europe and Asia Pacific produced 48.45%, 36.33% and 15.22% of FY2025 revenue, so the business is spread across two product groups and three regions, although lifecycle management is the larger group. End markets are industrials, aerospace and defense, electronics, automotive and medical technology.

Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_ptc-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-K_2025-09-30_ptc-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 76; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 21; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C18; calculation C19

The customer base is tied to discrete manufacturing, which the issuer describes as exposed to import tariffs, high interest rates, volatile exchange rates and supply chain disruption. This is the main cyclical channel into revenue, and the issuer says customers may respond by delaying or reducing purchases, reducing the number of subscriptions or delaying payments.
### Ownership and group structure

Ownership offers no sponsor-extraction channel, but control rights are not established. The company is widely held with a single class of common stock, no sponsor or controlling shareholder is identified in the filings, and the board and larger holders are described only in a proxy statement that is not supplied. Ptc Inc. is the issuer of the 2028 senior notes and the main borrower under the credit facility, and no subsidiary guarantor existed when the FY2025 annual report was filed, so lenders rely on the parent and on security for foreign-subsidiary borrowings.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_ptc-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-K_2025-09-30_ptc-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 88; Business & governance (CP-1A)
The buyer of Kepware and ThingWorx may owe further consideration of up to USD 125 million after a later sale of those businesses, which is an upside to cash that the issuer has not recognised.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue is predictable in its recurring part and lumpy in its license part. Support and cloud services were 53.63% of FY2025 revenue and are recognised over the contract term, while license revenue was 42.45% and is recognised when a contract starts, so it moves with contract timing: it grew 44.10% in FY2025 on larger and notably longer contracts and fell 18% in Q3 2026 on one renewal of shortened duration. Revenue grew 19.18% in FY2025, against annual run rate growth of 9.93%, and 11.64% in the nine months to June 2026, and the issuer cites commercial optimisation as a driver, but a price against volume split is not disclosed, so pricing power is not established.

Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_ptc-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-09-30_ptc-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-K_2025-09-30_ptc-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-K_2025-09-30_ptc-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 59; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 25; calculation C20; calculation C21; calculation C12; calculation C13; calculation C16

About 55% of revenue and about 30% of expenses are in currencies other than the US dollar, so a stronger dollar lowers reported revenue by more than it lowers expenses, although the effect was small in the nine months to June 2026, when revenue at constant currency would have been USD 9 million higher.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 25
### Cost structure and margin resilience

Margins are high and carry operating leverage in both directions. Gross margin was 83.76% of revenue in FY2025 and 83.45% in the nine months to June 2026, EBITDA margin was 39.61% and 36.77%, and operating expenses did not fall when Q3 2026 revenue fell, so operating income fell 20.65% on a 6.82% revenue decline. Stock-based compensation of 9.02% of revenue in the nine months to June 2026 is treated here as a cost.

Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_ptc-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 59; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C11; calculation C10; calculation C14; calculation C23

Cost flexibility appears limited in the short run. General and administrative expense rose 37.03% in the nine months to June 2026, mainly because acquisition and transaction costs rose from USD 2.4 million to USD 40.0 million, and Q3 2026 operating expenses were held flat partly by transition services income, which the issuer provides for up to 12 months from the sale. The share of fixed cost in the base is not disclosed, so the cost the issuer could remove in a downturn is not established.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation C22; calculation C35
### Capital intensity and cash conversion

Capital intensity is very low, so EBITDA turns into free cash flow at a high rate. Additions to property and equipment were 0.40% of FY2025 revenue and 0.79% in the nine months to June 2026, and free cash flow was 1.06x EBITDA in FY2024, 0.79x in FY2025 and 0.77x over the last twelve months. The issuer links a USD 179 million rise in long-term receivables in FY2025 to larger, longer contracts, which is one reason cash conversion fell. Capital expenditure offers little flexibility to protect cash because there is little to cut; the flexible uses of cash are repurchases and acquisitions.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_ptc-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-K_2025-09-30_ptc-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C24; calculation C7

FY2026 cash flow is burdened by divestiture items. The issuer guides about USD 100 million of cash taxes and about USD 50 million of costs on the sale, offset by about USD 70 million of free cash flow from the sold businesses, and cash interest of USD 60 million to USD 65 million; fourth-quarter operating cash flow is guided at only about USD 29 million after about USD 92 million of those cash taxes. Excluding the items the issuer says will not recur, guided FY2026 free cash flow would be about USD 950 million.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-07-29_ptc-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_ptc-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_ptc-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C25; calculation C27
### Market forces

Competitive rivalry is the force the filings document best. The issuer names Autodesk, Dassault Systèmes SA and Siemens AG as its main competitors in design and product lifecycle software, and it lists customers adopting competing solutions among its risks; switching costs and market shares are not quantified in the filings, so the strength of the moat is not established. Buyer power is limited by the absence of any customer above 10% of revenue, and the reseller channel is a minority of sales.

Economic and trade conditions are the macro factors that alter credit quality, through manufacturing demand, rates and currency, while political and social factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver on the sources supplied. Technology matters through the issuer's risk language on customers adopting competing solutions or being slow to adopt its artificial intelligence features. The risk language also names high interest rates and tightening credit as reasons for customers to delay purchases.
### Credit-translated SWOT
- Strengths: recurring revenue, high margins and cash conversion, low leverage and an undrawn revolver, all of which protect debt service.

### Financial profile and credit quality

The financial profile is strong and the trend is stable to slightly weaker. The main supports are recurring revenue, EBITDA margin of 36.77% in the nine months to June 2026, free cash flow of 0.77x EBITDA and net debt of 0.88x EBITDA, or 1.11x pro forma for the July 2026 repurchase; the constraints are the debt-funded repurchases, the fiscal 2028 concentration and the loss of the divested businesses. Lease obligations of USD 184,379 thousand sit outside the debt figure. The datapoints that would allow a firmer view are covenant levels, the balance sheet after July 2026, a retention rate and any issuer rating, none of which is supplied.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 19; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C4; calculation C7; calculation C10
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next 12 to 24 months the tailwind is growth in annual run rate, which the issuer guides at 9% to 9.5% in constant currency excluding divested businesses, and the headwinds are the removal of the sold businesses from revenue, the end of transition services income and rising interest cost on the July 2026 borrowing. Guided FY2026 free cash flow of about USD 850 million is about 1% lower than FY2025 and the issuer expects churn to stay low, which supports repayment capacity but not growth in it.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-07-29_ptc-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_ptc-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation C31

Over three to five years the central credit event is the 2028 refinancing. Replacing the 2028 notes at the 5.0% rate stated for the facility would add about USD 5.0 million a year of interest, which is small against EBITDA, so the refinancing is a question of market access and policy and not of affordability, provided the debt has not been raised by repurchases before then.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C33
### Downside scenario

The realistic downside starts with tariff-driven weakness among manufacturing customers, who delay purchases and shorten renewals. License revenue, which is recognised when a contract starts, falls first, as it did in Q3 2026 when revenue fell 6.82% and operating income fell 20.65% because operating expenses did not flex. Free cash flow then weakens, annual billing in advance means less cash is collected from smaller contract values, and if repurchases continue beyond free cash flow the revolver supplies the difference; drawing all of the amount available to borrow would take total debt to 1.79x EBITDA on the June 2026 amounts. Management can stop repurchases, which are discretionary, and capital expenditure is small, so resilience looks sufficient to avoid liquidity distress unless repurchases continue into the 2027 refinancing window.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-K_2025-09-30_ptc-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 36; calculation C14; calculation C32
Primary downside path: debt-funded repurchases continuing while renewal timing weakens revenue, ahead of the facility becoming current on 2027-01-03.
Basis: calculation C34; calculation C32
### Overall credit view

Overall, Ptc Inc. presents a strong business profile supported by recurring subscription revenue, high margins and low leverage, but credit quality is constrained by debt-funded repurchases and a single fiscal 2028 maturity window. Cash-flow durability appears strong because free cash flow was 0.77x EBITDA over the last twelve months and guided FY2026 free cash flow is about USD 850 million. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on whether net debt stays near the 0.88x EBITDA of June 2026, or the 1.11x pro forma for the July 2026 repurchase, until the facility becomes current on 2027-01-03. The primary downside path is repurchases funded by the revolver while revenue timing weakens results. Against typical leveraged-credit issuers in software, low leverage is a point of difference, but no peer set is supplied, so the comparison is not established. Further analysis would require the covenant terms, the balance sheet after July 2026 and a rating.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_ptc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 19; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_ptc-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 2; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C7; calculation C1; calculation C4; calculation C34
